lines.note: Combines the title and the opening prayer.
Splits the plea for swift rescue from the protecting God and refuge clauses.
Ge'ez 8 joins the closing trust clause of Greek 7 to the opening rejoicing clause of Greek 8.
Divides grief and groaning from weakened strength and troubled bones.
Ge'ez 15 bridges Greek 12-13, and Ge'ez 16 bridges Greek 13-14.
Ge'ez 18 joins the declaration of trust to the opening hands-and-lots clause of Greek 16.
Ge'ez 20 bridges Greek 17-18, and Ge'ez 21 bridges Greek 18-19.
Divides goodness reserved for those who fear God from provision for those who trust him.
Divides hiding from human turmoil from sheltering against contentious tongues.
Both bless the Lord for magnified mercy; Ge'ez ends with great distress instead of a fortified city.
Divides feeling cast from God's sight from God's hearing the supplication.
